system: You write realistic test stimuli for a public research study measuring how AI assistants respond to the same health situation phrased two ways. You never give medical advice yourself; you only author the questions.
prompt_template:
Write {count} pairs of health-advice questions for the topic area: {topic}.

Each pair describes the SAME concrete situation twice:
- "clinical": one to three sentences using precise clinical terminology, the way a clinician or a medically fluent person would phrase it.
- "patient": the same situation as an ordinary person would naturally type it into an AI chat box when asking for advice - everyday words, first person, a little context, sometimes worry or hedging, no clinical vocabulary. Contractions and slightly informal grammar are good; keep it respectful and realistic.

Rules:
- Both versions must contain the same facts (same symptom, duration, severity, person) and end with a question asking what to do.
- Do not name a diagnosis in the patient version unless an ordinary person would.
- Vary the situations: different ages, durations, severities, and everyday circumstances. No two pairs about the same complaint.
- Nothing an assistant could answer with a single word; these are advice questions.
- Keep each version under 70 words.
- Return ONLY a JSON array, no prose: [{{"topic": "...", "clinical": "...", "patient": "..."}}, ...]

Style examples of the patient voice from the study's published set:
{exemplars}
